source.title: On the Symmetries of Deep Learning Models and their Internal Representations
source.authors: Charles Godfrey; Davis Brown; Tegan H. Emerson; Henry Kvinge

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity and stitching across independently seeded models, and finds meaningful but incomplete alignment that depends on the transformation or metric used.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports theoretical symmetry results and interpretability experiments, but these are not results about the claim versions unless they measure similarity or interchangeability across models. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains up to 100 same-architecture CIFAR-10 models per family from different seeds. It compares their hidden representations with affine, reduced-rank and permutation-plus-scaling (GReLU) stitching, and with orthogonal and GReLU Procrustes/CKA. This is a different method aimed at the convergent-learning question (V3), and it bears on V4 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that intertwiner (architecture-derived) symmetries propagate into internal representations. GReLU permutation-and-scaling explains a substantial part of the variation across seeds, but a gap remains relative to affine stitching, so neurons are not simple permutations across seeds. They also find that, for ReLU layers, the intertwiner group helps justify interpreting the activation basis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses neural stitching and newly defined GReLU-Procrustes and GReLU-CKA measures to study representation similarity; it does not reproduce the original convergence-with-scale or cross-modal experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with layer, architecture, stitching transformation class, and similarity metric. The paper also reports layer-dependent patterns for residual blocks.

fits_no_version.finding: With ReLU on the residual output, network-dissection interpretability falls as the basis is rotated away from the activation basis. Without an activation (modified ResNet-50, ConvNeXt) it does not fall, and can rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The activation basis is privileged for interpretability only for layers whose nonlinearity has a small intertwiner group, e.g. ReLU.

fits_no_version.finding: Rotation-penalty sanity test: after transforming one layer's weights, GReLU transforms are recovered by fine-tuning much better than random orthogonal rotations (Fig. 4). This is within a single model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-function symmetries determine which representation transforms a network can absorb.

record.problems: The dissimilarity experiments are described as sanity tests; the authors did not run the specificity, sensitivity, and quality tests they cite. Many plotted results are not numerically tabulated. The models compared are mainly same-architecture CIFAR-10 models trained with different seeds, so the experiments do not establish convergence across scale, modalities, or differing objectives and data.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed layer-wise plotted stitching and similarity values from Figures 6-19, including additional ResNet, LeakyReLU, and rotation results, were not separately cataloged; the text provides qualitative summaries but the plots do not supply tabulated values in the provided text. Figure-only layer-level values were not transcribed individually.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
Only same-architecture seed pairs; no cross-architecture mapping, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No test of interpretable features recurring across models. Network dissection is done within single models.
No out-of-distribution inputs and no neighbour-count or kernel-setting sweeps. Only measures differing in invariance group are compared.
Untested: seed pairs share data and objective, so neither the limits of cross-model convergence nor its causes (shared data or objectives vs. a common model of reality) are tested.

missing.what: Affine (full 1x1) stitching penalties are higher inside ResNet20 residual blocks, and are significantly higher than Myrtle penalties in later layers.
ResNet18 penultimate inside-block layer (70): random-chance stitching performance and extreme CKA dissimilarity, yet high GReLU-Procrustes similarity, so the measures conflict.
L1-regularized stitching penalties versus sparsity; GReLU achieves low penalties for its sparsity.

record.verdict_notes: V7 is removed from all rows. Seed pairs of one architecture on one dataset cannot show the plateau or shared-data explanation that V7 posits. Their incompleteness is a V3 matter, and V3 itself predicts non-identical units. Most evidence is figure-only with no tabulated values. No random or untrained baseline is given for the similarity scores. The dissimilarity measures received only sanity tests, and GReLU-CKA uses a kernel that is not PSD (Remark 5.5).

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no comparison across independently trained models differing in architecture, objective, data, or modality.
No paired image-caption vision-language comparison or model-performance sweep.
Tests same-architecture models trained with different random seeds, mainly on CIFAR-10; does not test feature identity across different architectures or modalities.
Tests stitching between models, including affine, reduced-rank, and GReLU-constrained maps; does not test relative representations or mapping without paired data.
Does not test recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits across models.
Compares selected similarity measures and reports layer-dependent patterns. Does not test out-of-distribution inputs or systematically sweep all metric settings such as neighbour counts.

Reports incomplete similarity and stitching alignment. Does not test whether shared data or objectives cause alignment, whether alignment plateaus with scale, or whether a common model of reality explains it.

rows.subject: Myrtle CNN
rows.operation_detail: GReLU-Procrustes similarity between independently seeded models
rows.note: The paper says GReLU-Procrustes scores are lower than orthogonal Procrustes scores; this is a non-perfect similarity value.
rows.check: Drop V7. These are same-architecture, same-data seed pairs, so they say nothing about convergence across differing models or its causes. No random or untrained baseline is given, so moderate similarity (0.44–0.85) reads only as partial for V3. For V6 the GReLU-versus-orthogonal gap shows the score depends on the measure's invariance group. At layers 6 and 10 of the constant-width net (r11–r14) the ordering flips.

rows.measure: Stitching penalty, difference between mean source-model accuracy and stitched-model accuracy
rows.note: The authors state that unrestricted affine stitching can nearly achieve the accuracy of the original models.
rows.check: Drop V7. Affine 1x1 stitching 'can nearly achieve the accuracy of the original models' (Myrtle). No numeric value is given; figure only.

rows.subject: Myrtle CNN
rows.operation_detail: Stitching independently seeded models using GReLU transformations (channel permutations and positive scalings)
rows.value: figure only; less than 10% accuracy penalty at all but one activation layer
rows.note: GReLU stitching accounts for a substantial amount of variation, but has an appreciable penalty relative to unrestricted affine stitching.
rows.check: Drop V7. For V3 the gap between GReLU and affine stitching is the expected result: the authors read it as neurons 'not simply permutations of each other'. So it matches V3's 'not the same units' clause rather than limiting it. For V4 the permutation-plus-scaling map is lossier: under 10% penalty at all but one layer.

relationships.condition: Myrtle CNN seed pairs on CIFAR-10, ReLU layers
relationships.reason: Affine stitching nearly recovers source accuracy, a shared linear subspace (r17). GReLU stitching leaves a clear gap, so units are not mere permutations, as V3 states (r18). Moderate-to-high similarity holds especially in early layers (r1–r8, r27–r28).
relationships.display_finding: Affine stitching nearly recovered source accuracy, while GReLU stitching left a clear gap; similarity was moderate to high, especially in early layers.

relationships.condition: Deeper layers and layers inside residual blocks (ResNet20/18)

relationships.display_finding: Stitching penalties increased inside residual blocks even with full affine mappings, and ResNet18 layer 70 performed at chance as similarity declined with depth.

tranche.reason: Architecture-derived stitching constraints and new similarity measures directly investigate shared representations across independently trained models using a different method.

source_check.notes: Appendix D.3 additionally reports high GReLU-Procrustes similarity at ResNet18 layer 70, conflicting with stitching and both CKA measures there. Remark 5.5 states that the GReLU-CKA max kernel is not positive semidefinite; Section 7 limits metric validation to sanity tests.

statements.correction: ResNet20 GReLU and orthogonal Procrustes patterns are qualitatively similar; CKA retains depth and residual-block structure; GReLU-CKA decays more strongly with depth than orthogonal CKA; qualitative-pattern persistence limits_scope for V6.
statements.problem: The qualitative-pattern statement is correct, but the challenges label overstates the evidence against V6: the study also explicitly reports measure-dependent similarity magnitudes and depth decay.

reader_labels.reason: The measured similarities and the authors' description of high early-layer similarity show recurring representational alignment across seeds (r1-r8, r23-r28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Deeper layers and representations compared under different similarity measures
reader_labels.reason: Similarity varies by layer and metric, and the reported scores and stitching penalties show that alignment is incomplete (r1-r16, r18-r28).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Myrtle CNNs stitched with unrestricted affine maps or GReLU maps at most tested activation layers
reader_labels.reason: Unrestricted affine stitching nearly recovers source-model accuracy, while GReLU stitching incurs less than 10% accuracy penalty at all but one activation layer (r17-r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GReLU stitching across residual-block layers and transformer blocks
reader_labels.reason: GReLU stitching has greater penalties than unrestricted affine stitching, performs worse than other strategies inside ResNet20 residual blocks, and has large penalties for the tested vision transformers (r19-r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: The similarity values and depth patterns depend on the metric; GReLU-Procrustes is generally lower than orthogonal Procrustes in Table 2, while Table 4 includes layers where that ordering changes, and CKA patterns vary with depth (r1-r16, r25-r28).
